newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PISTONS CRUSH KNICKS FOR BIGGEST WIN IN SEVEN YEARS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PISTONS CRUSH KNICKS FOR BIGGEST WIN IN SEVEN YEARS.

text.p: Lindsey Hunter scored 28 points and Grant Hill recorded a triple-double as the Detroit Pistons posted their biggest victory in seven years, a 112-78 thrashing of the New York Knicks on Wednesday.
"It's as close as we've been this year to a perfect game," said Hill, who had 17 points, 11 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double of the season and 12th of his career.
Joe Dumars equalled the entire Knicks offensive output in the third quarter, scoring 15 of his 21 points as the Pistons outscored New York 31-15 in the period.
The high-flying Pistons won for the eighth time in nine games and moved 15 games over .500 for the first time since April 15, 1992, ending New York's seven-game winning streak in convincing fashion.

John Starks had 15 points and Charles Oakley added 14 for New York. Allan Houston, in his first game at Detroit since leaving for the Knicks as a free agent, was greeted with boos and finished with only two points.
"I expected a lot of boos, but I didn't know how harsh they would be," said Houston.
Said Detroit coach Doug Collins: "From the tip on down, our guys were great. Our guys had a championship look tonight."
In Milwaukee, Shaquille O'Neal scored 41 points and grabbed 13 rebounds, offsetting a 42-point night by Glenn Robinson, as the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Bucks 111-105.
Elden Campbell and Eddie Jones each scored 19 points and Nick Van Exel chipped in 18 points and 11 assists as Los Angeles won for the sixth time in seven games.
Robinson shot 63 percent (19-for-30) from the floor and Vin Baker added 25 points and 10 rebounds for Milwaukee.
A Campbell jumper broke a 98-98 tie and O'Neal scored the final four points of an 8-1 burst that gave Los Angeles a 106-99 lead.
In Orlando, Reggie Miller scored five of his 34 points in the second overtime to lead the Indiana Pacers to a 102-95 victory over the injury-plagued Magic.
Miller scored all four of Indiana's points in the first extra session, which ended in a 92-92 tie. He then scored the first five points of the second overtime.
The Magic missed their first nine shots of the second OT before Dennis Scott's three-pointer with 12 seconds to go.
Playing without injured leading scorer Penny Hardaway and Nick Anderson, Orlando led by 11 points after two quarters. But Indiana held the Magic to 31 points in the second half.
In Cleveland, Terrell Brandon scored 28 points and Chris Mills added 16 as the Cavailers posted a 99-81 victory over the undermanned New Jersey Nets.
Bob Sura chipped in 12 points as the Cavs beat the Nets for the 21st time in their last 23 meetings.

Kerry Kittles scored 12 of his 20 points in the first quarter for the Nets, who have lost four in a row. Kendall Gill added 16 and Khalid Reeves 14 points for New Jersey, which was without frontcourt starters Shawn Bradley and Jayson Williams.
In Phoenix, John Williams scored 22 points and Rex Chapman added four in the final 2:13 as the Suns beat the Washington Bullets 114-107.
Michael Finley had 22 points and Danny Manning contributed 16 and 10 rebounds for the Suns, who have not lost to the Bullets since March 9, 1988, a span of 17 straight wins.
Gheorge Muresan's free throws gave Washington a 107-103 edge. But Washington was held scoreless in the final 3:46.
Rod Strickland had 20 points and 11 assists Webber added 18 and 10 boards for the Bullets, who had their four-game winning streak snapped.
In Denver, Ervin Johnson scored 18 points and Antonio McDyess added 17 as the Nuggets snapped a 10-game slide with a 95-79 win over the injury-riddled Sacramento Kings.
Dale Ellis chipped in 14 for the Nuggets, who won for just the second time in 12 games under new coach Dick Motta.
Mitch Richmond scored 32 points for the Kings, who matched a league season-low by using just seven players.
The Kings played without point guard Tyus Edney (sprained right ankle) and forwards Billy Owens (injured ankle), Lionel Simmons (injured right knee) and Corliss Williamson (injured left calf).
In Portland, Sam Perkins had 25 points and nine rebounds and Shawn Kemp added 22 points as the Seattle SuperSonics beat the Trail Blazers 106-102.
Gary Payton had 19 points and six assists and Hersey Hawkins added 14 points for Seattle, which has won 12 of the last 15 meetings with their Pacific Division rivals.
Isaiah Rider scored 23 points and pulled down 11 rebounds and Kenny Anderson added 21 points and 11 assists for Portland, which suffered its third straight loss.

At Golden State, Joe Smith scored 19 of his 30 points in the first half and pulled down 12 rebounds as the Warriors raced to a 17-point lead and breezed to a 123-96 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves.
Latrell Sprewell added 25 points and Chris Mullin had 16 for Golden State, which snapped a four-game losing streak.
Tom Gugliotta scored 20 points, Kevin Garnett added 18 and rookie Stephon Marbury contributed 14 for Minnesota, which fell to 2-12 on the road.
